body: Yes, validation occurs after type casting. The typecasting is done when entities are marshalled because we need to correctly handle things like DateTime instances.
Thanks. So is it just that the `numeric` rule on strings is impossible when using `newEntity`? I understand why it's happening, but I don't know if it's something that can be fixed.

@markstory, sorry if this has been asked before, but should I just be using `new Entity()` directly instead of `Table->newEntity()` when doing things like `Controller::add()`? Is one preferred over the other? I noticed that when using the `Table` method the validation messages are also just the default ones in addition to the marshalling interfering with `numeric` validation. Everything work as expected when using `new Entity()`. I just don't know when I'd expect the `Table` method to be preferred.

The method is preferable imo, as the type casting is important for date/time types. It also uses a concrete entity class if available. We could try removing the casting from numeric types, but I think that might expose other issues.

A similar probably exists with Dates, it is entirely possible to set a entity date to an invalid date (such as 2014/02/30). The DateTime object silently fails by assuming you meant 2014/03/02 which means that a 'validDate' validation will always pass.

I don't know how we can reconcile marshalling complex types and also handle these kind of invalid data situations. Would it be useful if the marshaller raised an exception when marshalling specific types resulted in incorrect casting? For example if a date fails to 'deserialize' we could raise an exception.

I've been thinking about this some more and I totally agree that the marshaller casting values creates almost as many problems as it fixes. I think there may be a compromise though:
1. For basic types (string, integer, float) No casting should only be done types that are roughly the same type. For example, float and integer will only cast `is_numeric` data. Casting all values makes it impossible to validate data.
2. For complex types (date, time, datetime) will attempt to convert strings into Time instances, if that fails, the original value will be returned. There will still be some challenges as @dakota pointed out PHP will happily convert invalid dates into valid ones. Unless we require all dates to be in a specific format I don't see a way around this. If we required that all dates be in the input of `Y-m-d H:i:s` the marshaller could detect date shifts and return the string value.

I'm not sure this solves all the issues and it might create other ones, but it does help solve the issues described here, without totally removing the benefits marshalling provides (consistent types).

issue.body:
you cannot throw a validation error when date cannot be converted into valid datetime because php throws an internal error.

number validation is even more problematic because "floatval" is used to convert. If you pass for instance "F" in the field then it will be converted to "0" by "floatval" AND the validation doesn't fail. But it must fail of course. 
You can replace the decimal_point found in (http://php.net/manual/de/function.localeconv.php) by "." and the thousands_sep by "" and check via php "is_numeric".
